captureMethod: PostToolUse hook (matcher Read|Grep|Glob|Bash) writing raw stdin to a temp file, invoked via `claude --model claude-haiku-4-5 --dangerously-skip-permissions --tools "Bash,Read,Grep,Glob" -p <prompt>` against a throwaway temp project directory outside the repo.
sanitization: session_id, prompt_id, tool_use_id, transcript_path, cwd, and all absolute filesystem paths inside tool_input/tool_response were replaced with fixed placeholder values (00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000, /redacted/..., raw-capture-artifact.json). File and match content strings are the real (non-sensitive, author-authored) sample text; no secrets or real project paths are present.

read.json.notes: Confirms the plan's proposed path .tool_response.file.content is correct for this CLI version. tool_response also carries file.filePath, file.numLines, file.startLine, file.totalLines as required siblings.

grep-content.json.notes: output_mode:"content" returns tool_response.content as a plain string (ripgrep-style "file:line:text" lines). This matches the existing extractor's top-level .content string branch; no separate Grep-specific path was needed.

grep-files-with-matches.json.notes: output_mode:"files_with_matches" (the tool default) returns only mode/filenames/numFiles with no text field at all. There is nothing to compact for this shape; extraction is expected to fail (no .content/.text/.output) and the hook should fail open, which is existing/intended behavior, not a defect.

glob.json.notes: Glob tool_response returns filenames/durationMs/numFiles/truncated/totalMatches/countIsComplete with no text field. Same fail-open expectation as Grep files_with_matches.

bash.json.notes: DISCREPANCY FROM ASSUMPTION: this CLI version merges stdout and stderr into a single tool_response.stdout string; tool_response.stderr was observed as an always-empty string even when the command wrote to fd 2 only. Do not assume stderr is populated independently; compaction logic must treat stdout as the combined stream and treat stderr as possibly-empty even when the underlying command produced stderr output. Top-level duration_ms, tool_use_id, and session_id were present on capture (2.1.207) and reconfirmed on 2.1.260 (2026-09-04).

bash-background.json.notes: Captured after a PreToolUse hook injected hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput with run_in_background:true alongside the preserved command (compound sleep, not a bare long leading sleep). PROVEN: the CLI honors the injected flag. PostToolUse tool_input retains run_in_background:true; tool_response carries backgroundTaskId with empty stdout/stderr; duration_ms reflects launch time (~3.7s) rather than sleep wall clock; the model-visible result is a background shell id. Capture method matches this file's top-level captureMethod.

mcp-third-party.json.notes: Synthetic Cursor/Antigravity MCP PostToolUse payload for a third-party server. The hook must exit 0 and emit no output, leaving the result untouched.

mcp-ralph-proxy.json.notes: Synthetic Cursor/Antigravity MCP PostToolUse payload for a Ralph proxy tool. With RALPH_PROXY_SHELL_COMPACT=1 the hook must emit updated_mcp_tool_output and compact the oversized shell text.
